{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]

Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]

[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[皇學館大学]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000年}}}} {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Miyake Shrine Suzuka}} [[Category:Miyake {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[皇學館大学]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000年}}}} {{神道 横}} {{citation needed|Miyake Shrine Suzuka}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]

Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]

[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]

[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000年}}}} {{神道 横}} {{citation needed|Miyake Shrine Suzuka}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983年}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000年}}}} {{神道 横}} {{citation needed|Miyake Shrine Suzuka}}
