{{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{citation needed|Miyake Shrine Suzuka}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Miyake Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Shrines]] [[Category:bump1-19]] [[Category:refreshing categories imported on 2024-01-19]] [[Category:refreshing imported pages]] [[Category:second attempt at refreshing on January 27 2024]] [[Category:New]] [[Category:qq]] }} [[sn:Miyake Shrine]] [[ja:三宅神社]] [[sn:iyake Shrine]]

* [[屯倉神社]] - [[大阪府]][[松原市]]鎮座。 * [[三宅神社 (亀岡市)]] - [[京都府]][[亀岡市]]鎮座。 * [[三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] - [[三重県]][[鈴鹿市]]鎮座。
{{aimai}} {{デフォルトソート:みやけしんしや}} [[Category:同名の神社]]

[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en}} | established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]] }} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|en}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{citation needed|Miyake Shrine Suzuka}} {{draft categories| }} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Miyake Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:11]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Shrines]] [[Category:New]] }} [[sn:Miyake Shrine]] [[ja:三宅神社]] [[sn:iyake Shrine]] {{translated page|ja|三宅神社|version=102027241|comment=Imported full ja history}}

The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|三宅神社|version=102027241|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Miyake Shrine]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Shrines]] }} [[sn:Miyake Shrine]] [[ja:三宅神社]] [[sn:iyake Shrine]]

Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}|established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]]|qq=draft}} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka City|qq=}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mie Prefecture|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|三宅神社|version=102027241|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Shrines]] }} [[sn:Miyake Shrine]] [[ja:三宅神社]] [[sn:iyake Shrine]] [[Category:同名の神社]]

The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|三宅神社|version=102027241|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha|Shrines]] }} [[sn:Miyake Shrine]] [[ja:三宅神社]] [[sn:iyake Shrine]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]]

Former {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}|established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]]|qq=draft}} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka City|qq=}}, [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|三宅神社|version=102027241|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] }} [[sn:Miyake Shrine]] [[ja:三宅神社]] [[sn:iyake Shrine]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:pages without english wikidata name]] [[Category:Shikinaisha]][[sn:Miyake Shrine]][[Category:Shikinaisha]]

The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{translated page|ja|三宅神社|version=102027241|comment=Imported full ja history}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] }} [[sn:Miyake Shrine]] [[ja:三宅神社]] [[sn:iyake Shrine]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:pages without english wikidata name]] [[sn:Miyake Shrine]][[Category:qq]][[sn:Miyake Shrine]][[Category:qq]]

It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. {{afc comment|Wikidata entry [[d:Q45261980]] Wikidata name: (none) [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:16, 11 June 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox religious building|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]|religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]]| religious_affiliation = [[Shinto]] | name = Miyake Shrine | image = [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) haiden.JPG|280px]]
Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]]
[[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] | Status = {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Minor) [[論社]]
Presumed {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}
Former {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}|established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]]|qq=draft}} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka City|qq=}}, [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] }} [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:pages without english wikidata name]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[ja:三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}}

Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. Former {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}|established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]]|qq=draft}} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka City|qq=}}, [[:en:Mie Prefecture|Mie Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] }} [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[ja:三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}} [[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]]

The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] }} [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:qq]][[Category:qq]] [[ja:三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}} [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}} [[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]][[Category:LINKED FROM WIKIDATA DO NOT OVERWRITE]]
