The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] }} [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[ja:三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}}

The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} {{draft categories| }} [[ja:三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:pages with conflicting qids]]

It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:qq]]

Haiden | location = 1609 Kokufu-cho, Suzuka City, Mie Prefecture | coordinates = {{coord|34|51|16.18|N|136|30|25.92|E|region:JP-24_type:landmark|display=inline,title|name=Miyake Shrine}} | deity = [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]]

Former {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}|established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]]|qq=draft}} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka City|qq=}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|WD=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:qq]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:pages]]

It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}} [[Category: Completion tier 5]] [[Category:Disambiguation pages]] [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

Former {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}|established = Unknown | Main_hall = [[Nagare-zukuri]] | alternate_names = Sōja Daimyōjin | Rituals = [[October 10]]|qq=draft}} [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) torii.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Torii]] [[File:Miyake-jinja (Kou-cho, Suzuka) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|Honden]] '''Miyake Shrine''' ({{lang|ja|三宅神社}}, ''Miyake Jinja'') is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} in {{ill|Suzuka City|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka City|qq=}}, {{ill|Mie Prefecture|en|Mie Prefecture|qid=Q128196|lt=Mie Prefecture|1=Mie Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/式内社|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]], presumed to be the {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} of {{ill|Ise Province|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Province|qq=}}, and its modern shrine Rank was {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}}. The shrine absorbed the nearby {{ill|江神社|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/江神社|qq=}} (E Shrine) at the end of the {{ill|Meiji period|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji period|qq=}}, which was another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == Deities == The current enshrined deities are as follows:[http://www.amigo.ne.jp/~chitonr2/jinjaichiran_suzuka.html List of Shrines in Mie Prefecture > Suzuka City] (Mie Prefecture Shrine Association). * [[Kuni-no-Tokotachi|Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto]] * [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto]] - The deity of the absorbed 江神社. According to the Meiji-era shrine records, the enshrined deities were Kuni-no-Tokotachi-no-Mikoto, Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto, and [[Toyouke-Bime|Toyouke-Hime-no-Mikoto]]. Following the shrine mergers in the late Meiji period, a total of 24 deities are now enshrined. == History == The exact date of establishment is unknown. The shrine is mentioned in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in {{ill|927 AD|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/927 AD|qq=}}, as one of the shrines in {{ill|Suzuka District|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suzuka District|qq=}}, Ise Province, under the name "Miyake Shrine." It is considered a candidate {{ill|論社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/論社|qq=}} for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} of the same name. Another candidate is the Miyake Shrine in {{ill|Miyake Town|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miyake Town|qq=}}, Suzuka City, which is considered by some scholars to be the more likely location of the historical "Miyake Shrine" due to its proximity to the ancient imperial landholdings called "屯倉" (''miyake''). In the Edo period, the shrine was popularly known as "Sōja Daimyōjin" and was renamed "Miyake Shrine" during the Meiji Restoration. The name "Miyake" may reflect a connection to the ancient Ise provincial capital, possibly serving as the provincial {{ill|Sōja|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sōja|qq=}} during the late Nara to Heian periods. During the Meiji period, the shrine was designated as a {{ill|Village shrine|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village shrine|qq=}} in 1873. In 1908 and 1911, the shrine absorbed several smaller shrines in the area, including 江神社 (E Shrine), another {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} [[論社]]. == References == {{Reflist}} == Further Reading == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=式内社研究会|author=井後政晏|authorlink=井後政晏|chapter=三宅神社|year=1977|title=式内社調査報告 第7巻|publisher=[[Kogakkan University]]出版部|isbn=|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（式内社）|1977th year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1983|chapter=三宅神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 24 三重県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=978-4582490244|ref={{Harvid|三宅神社（平凡社）|1983rd year }}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=中世諸国一宮制研究会|author=|year=2000|chapter=|title=中世諸国一宮制の基礎的研究|publisher=岩田書院|isbn=978-4872941708|ref={{Harvid|一宮制|2000th year }}}} {{神道 横}} {{Sōja shrines}} [[ja:三宅神社 (鈴鹿市国府町)]] {{wikidata link|Q45261980}} [[Category:Ise Province|Shrines]] [[Category:Shikinaisha in Ise Province]] [[Category:Shinto shrines in Mie Prefecture]] [[Category:Shrine disambiguations]] [[Category:Son-sha]] [[Category:Suzuka, Mie]] [[Category:Sōja shrines]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]
